title: In Septem Pslamos Poenitentiales Expositio
author: Gregory the Great
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1306.tmp1306.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Et quia post mortem carnis alii aeternis deputantur suppliciis, et alii ad vitam per ignem transeunt purgationis ; 469 fide lis anima non solum furorem timet, sed etiam iram abhorret, teste beato Augustino : Hi omnes qui non posuerunt sibi fundamentum Christum, in furore arguuntur, quia æterno igne cruciantur. Qui autem eidem fundamento superposuerunt lignum, fenum, stipulam, in ira corripiuntur; quia igne purgati, ad beatitudinis requiem (a)deducuntur(I Cor.
passages.english: And because after the death of the flesh some are assigned to eternal punishments, and others pass through the fire of purgation to life, the faithful soul not only fears [God's] fury but also shrinks from [his] anger, as blessed Augustine bears witness: All those who did not lay Christ as their foundation are rebuked in fury, because they are tormented by eternal fire. But those who built wood, hay, stubble upon that same foundation are chastised in anger, because, having been purged by fire, they are led to the rest of blessedness (1 Cor.
passages.notes: The '469' before 'fidelis' is a page number from the printed edition and has been left out; '(a)' is a footnote mark. The biblical reference is cut off at the end of the passage and continues in the following text ('111)', apparently for 1 Cor. 3).

passages.original: Sunt enim plerique qui, etsi peccata sua fletibus puniant, pauperes tamn opprimere potestatis suae dominatione non cessant, Hinimirum nequaquam purum sacrificium Deo offerunt: quia detestabilis superbiæ illud admistione corrumpunt. Vel sicut beatus Hieronymus [In hune psalm. ] hunc locum exponit, illi cor conterunt, sed non humiliant, qui peccata quidem quæ commiserunt deflent, sed tamen eadem committere etiam post fletus non timeni. Dum enim errorum Moram consideratione revocati, ad ea quæ dimiserant redeunt, se contra conditorem suum per opera pravi- tatis extollunt.
passages.english: For there are many who, although they punish their sins with weeping, nevertheless do not cease to oppress the poor by the domination of their power. These, without doubt, by no means offer a pure sacrifice to God, because they corrupt it by mixing in detestable pride. Or, as blessed Jerome [On this psalm] expounds this passage, those crush their heart but do not humble it who weep indeed for the sins they have committed, yet even after their weeping are not afraid to commit the same [sins]. For while, called back [from sin] by considering the delay of their errors, they return to what they had given up, they exalt themselves against their Creator through works of wickedness.
passages.notes: 'errorum Moram consideratione revocati' is obscure, and possibly corrupt; 'Moram' (delay) may be a misreading, perhaps for 'malum' or 'molem' ('the weight of their errors'). It is translated literally.

passages.original: Sicut namque Christus, qui est caput Ecclesiae, de Spiritu sancto conceptus est, sic sancta Ecclesia quae corpus ejus est, eodem Spiritu sancto repletur ut vivat; ejus virtute firmatur, ut in unius fidei et charitatis compage subsislat. Undedicit Apostolus: Ex quo totum corpus pernexus et conjunctiones subministratum et constructum crecit in augmentum Dei (Col. II, 2). Istud est corpus, extra quod non vivificat spiritus. Unde dicit beatus Augustinus : Si vis vivere de spiritu Christo, esto in corpore Christi [Tract. i6 in Joan.]. De hoc spiritu non vivit haereticus, non vivit schismaticus, non vivit excommunicatus ; non enim sunt de corpore.
passages.english: For just as Christ, who is the head of the Church, was conceived of the Holy Spirit, so the holy Church, which is his body, is filled with the same Holy Spirit so that it may live; it is strengthened by his power, so that it may stand firm in the bond of one faith and charity. Hence the Apostle says: From whom the whole body, supplied and built up through joints and connections, grows to the increase of God (Col. 2:2). This is the body outside of which the spirit does not give life. Hence blessed Augustine says: If you wish to live by the spirit of Christ, be in the body of Christ [Tractate 26 on John]. The heretic does not live by this spirit, the schismatic does not live [by it], the excommunicate does not live [by it]; for they are not of the body.
passages.notes: The verse quoted is Col. 2:19; the edition's reference 'II, 2' is probably defective. 'i6' is taken as 26, the usual numbering of Augustine's tractate.

passages.original: et jam quasi non sint quod fuerant, dum in aliam mutati naturam, in lumine claritatis Dei perenniter exsultant. Solus namque Deus vere immortalis est, quia solus æternus et incommutabilis est. Unde dicit beatus Augustinus ; Vera aeternitas et vera immortalitas non est nisi in Deitate Trinitatis, cui quod est esse perfectum est; quia natura initio carens, incremento non indigens, sicut nullum finem, ita nullam recipit mutabilitatem.
passages.english: and now [they are] as though they were not what they had been, since, changed into another nature, they rejoice everlastingly in the light of God's brightness. For God alone is truly immortal, because he alone is eternal and unchangeable. Hence blessed Augustine says: True eternity and true immortality exist only in the Godhead of the Trinity, for whom to be is to be perfect; because, being a nature lacking a beginning and needing no increase, just as it admits no end, so it admits no mutability.
